newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni Q1 97 net profit drops.
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni Q1 97 net profit drops.

text.p: Czech Komercni Banka a.s. said on Wednesday its unaudited net profit for the first quarter eased slightly due to increased provisioning for loans to clients under bankruptcy proceedings.

Komercni, the country's largest commercial bank, said its net profit, calculated according to international accounting standards, dipped to 1.04 billion crowns ($33.6 million) for the first quarter from 1.348 billion a year ago.
Under Czech accounting standards, the bank's net profit slipped to 868 million crowns in the period from 1.36 billion.
"The results are in line with the expectations of the management," Deputy General Director Borivoj Prazak told journalists.
"We consider them to be adequate to the situation of the bank and to the economic situation, and evaluate them as positive," he added.
Komercni shares slipped 39 crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange after the results announcement to close at 2,186.

Reserves stood at 26.6 billion at the end of March, up from 25.6 billion at the end of 1996. Provisioning for loan losses increased to 1.37 billion in the first quarter from 1.07 billion for the same period of 1996, the bank said.

Komercni's net interest margin slipped to 3.45 percent at the end of March from 3.95 percent at the end of 1996. Deputy Director Petr Budinsky said this was a result of the bank's policy of orientation on highly secure clients.

Komercni's balance sheet total dropped to 443.919 billion crowns from 446.019 billion at the end of 1996, which Budinsky said was a seasonal phenomenon. Comparative IAS balance sheet total for the first quarter of 1996 was not available.
Komercni did not give any forecast for full-year results.

It also said in a statement that it would lower its basic lending rate, the reference rate, by 20 basis points to 12.05 percent on May 5. It said this cut was a result of the development of rates on the interbank market.
The six-month Prague interbank offered rate (PRIBOR), from which the reference rate is derived, stood at 12.04 percent on Wednesday, up four basis points from Tuesday.
